patterns: APPSC asks single-fact items: dengue lowers platelets, filariasis (lower-limb swelling), Fasciola invades liver, Gambusia for malaria control, ringworm = fungi, brucellosis = bacteria, air pollution hits respiratory system.
Odd-one-out 'vector is not a mosquito' (leishmaniasis/kala-azar, sleeping sickness, plague) and 'not water-borne' (kwashiorkor, TB, hepatitis B, fluorosis) recur across PSCs.
Pathogen-type classification (virus/bacteria/protozoa/fungus) and bird flu H5N1 vs swine flu H1N1 are frequent; other PSCs add Fleming-penicillin, Waksman, Widal/Mantoux tests.
Recent APPSC Forest papers add livestock diseases (FMD, bovine TB, Chagas vector) and State of Global Air figures.

App MCQs are heavy on long 4-6 statement 'about X disease' sets and match lists built from note tables; APPSC is far more direct. AMR/One Health/AP data items have little PYQ backing but are sound current-affairs angles.
